channel.title: Factory Droid Research
channel.description: Research articles from Factory about coding agents, agent harnesses, and evaluation.

item.title: Droid 1.0: Building a Frontier Harness
item.description: A new engine powering Factory's enterprise agent, built for complex projects and everyday development.

item.title: What it Takes for Coding Agents to Complete Large Software Tasks
item.description: Held to a standard of completion they wrote themselves, agents rebuilt complex programs to near-parity.

item.title: Why model routing must be in the harness
item.description: Droid’s model routing cut cost 58% without lowering quality. Only the harness can judge when a model switch is worth the cache miss; the harness fits the job and the model to each other; and task outcomes improve later routing.

item.title: Deferred Context Engine
item.description: Droid keeps internal tools, MCP tools, skills, and plugins reachable without loading every schema on every turn. Production telemetry quantifies estimated input-token savings by catalog size.

item.title: Which Model Reviews Code Best?
item.description: We benchmarked 13 models to find the best price-performance tradeoff for AI code review.

item.title: How Missions Work
item.description: The architecture behind Missions: why agent context shapes every design decision, how separation of concerns and test-driven development at two levels produce reliable multi-day autonomous work, and how the system actually runs.

item.title: Legacy-Bench: Can AI Agents Maintain the World's Most Critical Software?
item.description: A new benchmark designed to measure frontier AI agent capabilities on legacy software engineering tasks spanning COBOL, Fortran, Java 7, and more.

item.title: Signals: Toward a Self-Improving Agent
item.description: How we built a closed-loop system for recursive self-improvement—where the agent detects its own failures and implements fixes automatically.

item.title: Let Me Droid That For You: What 780K Agent Searches Reveal
item.description: Droid analyzed 780,000 of its own web searches. It wrote the queries, built the pipeline, and generated the visualizations.

item.title: Evaluating Context Compression for AI Agents
item.description: We built an evaluation framework to measure how much context different compression strategies preserve. After testing three approaches on real-world, long-running agent sessions spanning debugging, code review, and feature implementation, we found that structured summarization retains more useful information than alternatives from OpenAI and Anthropic.

item.title: The Droid Wars: Breaking up an AI‑orchestrated cyber fraud campaign
item.description: How we detected and disrupted a highly automated cyber operation that attempted to turn our AI software development platform into a node within a worldwide mesh of off‑label LLM usage.

item.title: Compressing Context
item.description: LLMs attend only to the tokens in their current prompt. Because every model enforces a finite context window, extended conversations and multi-step workflows eventually exceed that limit. Our strategy for retaining, selecting, and compressing prior turns is a major lever on inference quality, latency, and cost.

item.title: Building AI for Safe and Responsible Autonomy: Our Readiness Policy
item.description: Our mission at Factory is to bring autonomy to software engineering in a way that prioritizes safety, responsibility, and transparency.
